adjoini.essence: it is the exact sub-fact that keeps the root discriminant small: the new field stays within a factor of two
adjoini.statement: adjoining i to a number field changes the relative discriminant by a factor that divides four, only the prime two can ramify since x squared plus one gets a double root only in even residue characteristic, and so the root discriminant of the new field is at most twice the old one

apbound.essence: it keeps the base discriminant small: the log of the relative discriminant stays O of l log l
apbound.statement: the product of the first l primes that are one mod three grows like e to the O of l log l

charcutout.essence: it is the exact sub-fact that gives the base discriminant: conductor multiplicity for coprime conductors
charcutout.statement: an order three character cuts out the unique cyclic cubic subfield fixed by its kernel, and for characters whose conductors are pairwise coprime the conductors multiply, which is why the discriminant of the base field is the square of the product of the ramified primes

chebot.essence: it is the existence engine — the primes that split the way the tower needs, with the bad ones excluded
chebot.statement: chebotarev's density theorem says the primes whose frobenius class is a prescribed element exist in infinitely many, and the finitely many ramified primes may be excluded

classbound.essence: it is the pigeonhole door — a bounded class group makes the many norm-one elements pile up into few classes
classbound.statement: the class group of a number field has order at most the max of two and the root discriminant raised to an absolute constant times the degree, so fields of bounded root discriminant and bounded degree have class groups of bounded size

cmunit.essence: it is the shape of the norm-one set — the unit-length lattice the window probes for
cmunit.statement: an element that multiplies with its conjugate to one has absolute value one in every complex embedding, it sits on the unit circle in every view, and the integer check in the ring with i is that three squared plus four squared is five squared

cyclotomic.essence: it is the base of the tower — l independent cubic pieces whose galois group has l generators
cyclotomic.statement: for each prime r that is one mod three there is a unique totally real cyclic cubic subfield of the r-th cyclotomic field with conductor r, and for ramified primes that are pairwise coprime the cubic fields are linearly disjoint, the galois group of their compositum is l products of z over three, and its part over the base is the same with one generator removed

discrim.essence: it is the bookkeeping that keeps the tower's arithmetic small at every level
discrim.statement: the absolute discriminant of a tower multiplies up the levels by the norm of the relative discriminant, the root discriminant is the discriminant raised to the reciprocal of the degree, and a step that ramifies nowhere does not change the root discriminant

fratin.essence: it is the bookkeeping of generators — d of a group is the number of its independent directions
fratin.statement: burnside's basis theorem reads the generator count of a pro three group off its frattini quotient, and killing generators in the frattini quotient keeps the generator count fixed while the relation count grows by at most the number killed

gstest.essence: it is the engine that turns many generators and few relations into an infinite group
gstest.statement: the golod shafarevich test says a pro three group on d generators with r relations is infinite whenever r is at most d squared divided by four, and it is silent when r is above

hajir.essence: it is the meta lemma of the arithmetic half — the criterion the geometric lemma feeds into
hajir.statement: the hajir maire tower method says an infinite tower of unramified extensions of a totally real field exists when the generator count outgrows the relation cap at the levels, with the class group contribution controlled by the pigeonhole bound

minkembed.essence: it is the coordinate map that turns norm bounds into lattice point counts
minkembed.statement: the minkowski embedding sends a field of degree f into f dimensional complex space, and the product of the conjugates of an element is the square root of the absolute value of its norm

mod4minusone.essence: it is the arithmetic door — many primes of the right shape split at both steps of the tower
mod4minusone.source_lines: eq. (2) region (L280–295); square tables = the house bed
mod4minusone.statement: x squared plus one equals zero modulo an odd prime q has a solution exactly when q is one modulo four, and it feeds the tower: when q is one mod four and splits in the lower field then q splits in the field with i adjoined, since x squared plus one splits over the residue field

numberfields.essence: it is the ground under the whole tower — embeddings, the totally real condition, and the integer norm fact the packing step cites
numberfields.statement: a number field is a finite extension of the rationals, its embeddings into the complex numbers are all different, a field is totally real when every embedding lands in the reals, and the norm of a nonzero algebraic integer is a nonzero integer of absolute value at least one

primesplit.essence: it names the bad primes — the finite set every source statement must exclude
primesplit.statement: a rational prime in a field extension either splits into several distinct primes, stays inert, or ramifies, and the ramified primes are exactly the ones that divide the discriminant, a finite list

shafbound.essence: it caps the relation count against the generator count — the upper line of the golod shafarevich comparison
shafbound.statement: shafarevich's bound says that for a totally real cubic base field without the cube roots of unity the relation count of its maximal unramified pro three extension is at most the generator count plus an absolute constant c zero
